speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing progressive difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech difficulties. To help me narrow down the cause, have you noticed if your symptoms are worsening rapidly over weeks or gradually over months?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: ALS (Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis).

The combination of progressive upper and lower motor neuron signs—specifically the triad of gait difficulty, urinary incontinence, and bulbar symptoms (speech slurring)—in a 54-year-old male with a subacute course is highly suggestive of ALS.

REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Cervical_Spine and MRI Lumbar_Spine to rule out compressive myelopathy or normal pressure hydrocephalus.
